CRITIQUE_POINTS:
1) Mechanism label misuse risk: The rationale argues “TICT-like” primarily from “high flexibility / rotor potential” (E8, E54), but TICT specifically implies a twisted charge-transfer state. Your own priors say donor/acceptor topology is weak (E8) and there is no donor–acceptor pairing basis (E50), which undercuts a TICT claim more than the writeup acknowledges. A rotor-driven nonradiative channel can explain AIE without being TICT; within the allowed label pool this maps more naturally to “neutral aromatic” (LE + RIR) unless CT evidence appears.
2) Under-utilized evidence about aromatic/LE character: The aromatic_localization_score indicates “locally retained aromatic character” (E53), but the narrative treats “neutral aromatic” as a lower-priority fallback rather than a positively supported alternative. E53 is one of the few high-reliability, mechanism-informative cues available in R0.
3) Missing adjudication of contradictory neighbor signals: The text says neighbors are not decisive because top1_sim < 0.55 (E4) and entropy is high (E55/E6), yet the pack contains a compact-prior neighbor profile showing ESIPT majority with entropy 0.0 and multiple similarity=1.0 neighbors in that compact-metric space (compact_prior_neighbor_profile_v1, not referenced in the narrative). Even if you ultimately reject ESIPT via E51/E52, this conflict should be explicitly called out and resolved as “label noise / metric mismatch” rather than ignored.
4) ESIPT downweighting is structurally consistent but needs stronger explanation: “No PT site/readiness” (E51, E52) is a strong, concrete anti-ESIPT argument.
